title: Isandro and the Colony
premise: Edmund Ravensworth, a terraformer who has spent fifteen years quietly hauling cargo through contested orbits, is the first to board the Meridian when it returns from deep space with its crew aged backward into children. The discovery forces his hidden colony of deserters and refugees out of hiding, because the ship carries proof that Earth's government engineered the time anomaly as a weapon. To end the war before Earth's final transmission loop expires, Edmund must deliver that proof to both fleets — knowing whichever side receives it second will call him a traitor. In the end he splits the message between two found-family couriers, forcing an armistice neither government wanted but neither can refuse.
about_author: Sebastian Ashgrove is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent a decade writing technical manuals for interplanetary freight routes. They now write fiction about the people those manuals never mentioned.

chapters.title: The Garden for Unborn Hands
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He tends the terraforming greenhouse on Ceres Station, planting trees whose fruit will ripen decades after anyone currently alive could taste them. A routine cargo run brings him past the derelict beacon where the Meridian is due to return. Emotional beat: quiet devotion to a future he'll never see, establishing his patience and loneliness.

chapters.title: Children in Vacuum Suits
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The Meridian docks, and its veteran crew emerges aged backward — adults now children, memories intact. Among them is Captain Oyelaran, now nine years old, still giving orders in her captain's voice. Edmund realizes the anomaly's signature matches classified weapons research he saw during his military years. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Oyelaran's POV. She recounts the deep-space mission: they found a research station where Earth's navy was testing temporal displacement as a siege weapon, and she ordered the evidence copied before fleeing home. Flashbacks reveal Edmund's own desertion fifteen years ago. Emotional beat: two fugitives recognizing each other's guilt and resolve.

chapters.title: The Colony That Doesn't Exist
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He must tell his fellow colonists — smugglers, defectors, families who fled the war — that their invisibility is over. Some want to destroy the evidence and stay hidden; others, led by engineer Priya Kaur, argue silence makes them complicit. Emotional beat: found family fracturing under its first real test.

chapters.title: What the Navy Left Behind
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. A salvage run to the abandoned research station confirms the weapon tests killed thousands in the outer colonies, disguised as reactor failures. The team recovers the full data archive but triggers a silent alarm. Emotional beat: grief and fury hardening into purpose; the colony stops being victims and becomes witnesses.

chapters.title: Hunters in Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Both Earth's navy and the colonial fleet dispatch ships to seize the Meridian. The colony's patched-together convoy runs the blockade through a debris field, losing their oldest hauler and its pilot, old Vasquez, who stays behind to buy time. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal; Edmund questions whether truth is worth blood.

chapters.title: The Transmission Loop
chapters.summary: Oyelaran's POV. Earth announces its last scheduled transmission loop before wartime encryption changes permanently — a deadline after which no independent broadcast can reach either fleet. The colony has one window. Edmund proposes splitting the evidence: half to each fleet, so neither can weaponize it alone. Emotional beat: desperate hope tempered by the knowledge that both sides may simply shoot the messengers.

chapters.title: Two Couriers
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The colony votes. Priya takes the colonial-bound copy aboard the refitted Meridian crewed by the de-aged sailors, while Edmund flies alone toward Earth's fleet. Farewells at the dock are understated, unfinished. Emotional beat: found family choosing trust over control — sending their truth out in other people's hands.

chapters.title: The Verdict of Fleets
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Edmund reaches Admiral Chen's flagship and is nearly executed as a spy until the de-aged crew's testimony transmits live from Priya's side; the simultaneous arrival makes denial impossible. When a naval officer attempts to destroy the archive, the child-crew of the Meridian broadcasts it fleet-wide themselves. Emotional beat: climax — courage of the small and overlooked forcing giants to stop.

chapters.title: Seeds Already Planted
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. An armistice holds, uneasy and incomplete; the war-crimes tribunal convenes with Oyelaran testifying in her child's body. Edmund returns to Ceres and finds the greenhouse thriving — colonists stayed, tended it, planted more. The garden will feed people born after the war. Emotional beat: resolution — justice outside the law achieved at cost, survival paid for, family kept.
